basics.summary: Predator pushes Lead down to 0; Prey pushes it up to 10. Each round both secretly pick a Strategy, make an opposed check with the Strategy modifier, and the winner takes Advantages.
steps: Step 1: Choose Strategies (secretly; requirements must be met)
Step 2: Opposed Skill Check (reveal, apply modifiers; winner crit or loser crit failure shifts Lead 1 toward the winner)
Step 3: Resolution (winner picks 1 Advantage from his Strategy, +1 per 4 by which he won; check Lead for victory)
notes: Conflict continues while Lead is 1 to 9.
Several characters on one side make cooperative checks and gain a synergy bonus from Tactics.
A Strategy cannot be withdrawn once chosen; a participant may concede, giving the opponent his victory result.
Threats and errors have no effect beyond what each Conflict specifies; criticals only affect Lead and Conflict conditions.

advantages.name: Attack
advantages.summary: Winner gets +4 on attack checks against other chase participants for 1 full round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: +2 more and +1 threat range on those attacks.

advantages.name: Crisis
advantages.summary: An obstacle appears: every participant makes a Maneuver check vs. the current Crisis DC (Table 6.1) or crashes. A participant may skip the check, giving the opponent 3 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick lowers the winner's own Crisis DC by 5 (minimum 10).

advantages.name: Defense
advantages.summary: Winner gets +4 Defense against attacks from other chase participants for 1 full round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: +2 more and +1 error range on attacks against the winner.

advantages.name: Impact
advantages.summary: Winner and one chosen opponent both take collision damage (vehicle: equal to the opponent's check result; both on foot: 1d4 lethal). With GC approval passengers may attempt an Acrobatics/Jump (5 ft.) onto the target vehicle.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick reduces the winner's own damage by 4 (on foot vs. foot: +1d4 lethal each).

advantages.name: Lead
advantages.summary: Lead moves 1 point toward the winner.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks in the round move Lead 1 more point toward the winner, or instead remove 1 Smash point from an opponent.

advantages.name: Pause
advantages.summary: Conflict freezes: Lead stays put and no steps resolve next round, though Step 4 actions still happen.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds 1 more paused round.

advantages.name: Room
advantages.summary: Maneuvering Room shifts 1 grade in the direction the winner chooses.
advantages.repeat: Chosen 3 times in a round: winner sets Maneuvering Room to any grade.

advantages.name: Stress
advantages.summary: Everyone except the winner takes 1d4 stress damage that cannot be recovered until the chase ends.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds +1d4 stress damage.

advantages.name: Swap
advantages.summary: Predator and Prey trade roles, then Lead increases by 1.

advantages.name: Twist
advantages.summary: Winner may use Blend (Dex), Bluff (Cha), Impress (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Mechanics (Int), Sense Motive (Wis) or Streetwise (Wis), without tags, for the next opposed check.

advantages.name: Victory
advantages.summary: Conflict ends immediately in the winner's favor.

victory.predator: Leaders stop adjacent; Prey vehicle is immobilized; Predator side gets a half-action surprise round and may first apply 1 Impact Advantage to the Prey.
victory.prey: Prey and team get away and cannot be found for the rest of the scene; Prey may apply 1 Crisis Advantage to the Predator.

chase.outsideActions: Each driver or runner gets 1 half action; every passenger gets a full action or 2 half actions. Run alongside combat, these fall on each character's Initiative Count.

maneuveringRoom.title: Table 6.1: Maneuvering Room
rows: Open (e.g. light traffic, open skies, calm seas, etc.)
Close (e.g. moderate traffic, canyon flying, rough seas, etc.)
Crowded (e.g. heavy traffic, canyon flying with many intervening ledges, turbulent seas, etc.)
Tight (e.g. rush hour traffic, aerial dogfight, tsunami seas, etc.)
notes: * Everyone travels at this fraction of the slowest vehicle's top MPH (rounded down); mostly matters for crashes.
** Bonus to all chase Maneuver checks for whoever pilots the vehicle with the highest top MPH.
† DC of the Maneuver check required each time a crisis occurs.

chaseLead.title: Table 6.2: Chase Lead
notes: * May voluntarily drop to as little as 200 ft. per point to engage other aircraft.
** Ships can only effectively chase or fight other ships; Ship vs. Ship rounds last 2 minutes.
On foot, Acceleration = Strength modifier and Turning = Dexterity modifier (each minimum 0); otherwise the vehicle supplies both ratings.
GC sets Maneuvering Room (Open/Close/Crowded/Tight) at the start; it can change via the Room Advantage.
Chained chases: track a separate Lead per Predator/Prey pair and resolve each step pair by pair from front to back.
Mismatched vehicles: distance per Lead point is the shortest of those involved; if one vehicle's distance is more than double another's, resolve with a single opposed check instead.
Each chase round burns 1 minute of fuel. A pilot firing vehicle weapons uses the multi-tasking rules.
With simultaneous combat: Step 1 before the first Initiative Count, Steps 2-3 at the (first) Predator's count, Step 4 spread across the round.

Smash points (powered aircraft only): the single pilot 200+ ft. above the nearest opponent with no enemy above holds 1 per Lead point to the next highest opponent; +1 when he wins an opposed check or scores a Maneuver threat, -1 when another participant does; lost entirely at 0 or when conditions lapse.

Spending Smash after winning an opposed check: Predator spends 1 to reduce Lead by 1; Prey spends 1 for +4 Defense until his next Initiative Count. Attacks on a Smash holder add his Smash points to Lead when working out range.
Crash: on foot 1d4 lethal; vehicles take collision damage by size and speed, occupants make a Reflex save (DC half that damage) or take half. Crashed participants leave the chase.
“That’s Impossible!” winner spends 1 use of the class ability to choose any 1 Advantage, +1 per 4 margin, never Victory.

brainwashing.predator: Character(s) trying to break a captive's will
brainwashing.roundTime: 4 hours (mental approach) or 2 days (physical approach); see brainwashingApproaches table

Computed starting Lead is 10 or more

advantages.name: Alter Memory
advantages.summary: Prey gains or loses all memory of 1 event of up to 1 hour, chosen by the Predator.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick affects 1 more event of up to 1 hour.

advantages.name: Crisis
advantages.summary: Both sides make a Fortitude or Will save (DC 10 + half opponent's career level, rounded up). Failure: 1d3 temporary Wis and 1d3 temporary Cha damage; if only one side fails, the other wins. A side may skip the save, giving the opponent 3 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick lowers the winner's own Crisis DC by 2 (minimum 5).

advantages.name: Haste
advantages.summary: Next Conflict round takes half the standard time (rounded down, minimum 5 minutes).
advantages.repeat: Each further pick halves the duration again.

advantages.name: Lead
advantages.summary: Lead moves 1 point toward the winner.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks in the round move Lead 1 more point toward the winner.

advantages.name: New Approach
advantages.summary: Predator's approach flips between mental and physical.

advantages.name: Pause
advantages.summary: Conflict freezes: Lead stays put and no steps resolve next round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds 1 more paused round.

advantages.name: Revelation
advantages.summary: Winner may voluntarily disclose 1 fact about his organization (full history, an unknown goal, an unknown Rating, or an unknown Site) to gain 1 bonus action die.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: 1 more disclosure for 1 more bonus action die.

advantages.name: Shred
advantages.summary: The Prey's lowest-rated cover identity loses 1 Power Rating; at 0 the identity is blown.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks remove 1 more point, rolling over to the next-lowest identity if one hits 0.

advantages.name: Slip
advantages.summary: Winner either pulls 1 clue/secret from an opponent or passes off 1 lie as if a Bluff/Deception check with up to -6 penalty had succeeded.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: 1 more clue/secret, or lie penalty cap rises by 2 (-8, -10...).

advantages.name: Splinter
advantages.summary: Next round the Prey group must make a team check using its lowest skill bonus.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick extends this by 1 more round.

advantages.name: Stress
advantages.summary: Everyone except the winner takes 1d4 stress damage that cannot be recovered until the brainwashing attempt ends.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds +1d4 stress damage.

advantages.name: Twist
advantages.summary: Winner may use Analysis (Wis), Cultures (Int), Falsify (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Investigation (Cha), Science (Int) or Tactics (Int), without tags, for the next opposed check.

advantages.name: Victory
advantages.summary: Conflict ends immediately in the winner's favor.

victory.predator: Prey forgets the brainwashing itself; Predator either permanently erases 1 event of up to 24 hours, or compels 1 action as if an Impress/Persuasion check with up to -18 penalty succeeded (never one that would expose the Prey).
victory.prey: Prey proves resistant: the same Predator (or his group) cannot brainwash him again this mission.

brainwashingApproaches.title: Table 6.4: Brainwashing Approaches
notes: * Left of slash applies to the Predator's opposed check / error range; right of slash applies to the Prey's.
Predator picks a mental or physical approach at the start; it changes only through the New Approach Advantage.
Predator must be present for at least half of each round; the Prey is present throughout.
Several participants form a Predator group and a Prey group; each group makes one cooperative opposed check per round.
Each strategy names the skill used for that round's opposed check ("skill" field); alternate skill checks have no tags.
Prey save-bonus requirements use base Will vs. a mental approach and base Fortitude vs. a physical approach.
NPC career level, where a DC needs it, defaults to the team's current Threat Level.
Altered memories can be undone by a Medicine/Therapy Complex Task: 5 Challenges, 1 hour each, DC 20 + brainwasher's Manipulate bonus; failure blocks further attempts this mission.

hacking.name: Hacking
hacking.roundTime: Variable: set by current Lead, External vs. Internal Access and relative computer Power Ratings (see hackTiming tables)

startingLead.summary: Equal to the target system's Security Power Rating (maximum 9); with a previously installed back door, the Lead at which it was installed + 1.

rules.when: Predator has a back door in the system

strategies.summary: Fire viruses to cripple or commandeer the intruder's machine.

advantages.name: Back Door
advantages.summary: Predator either removes one of the Prey's silhouettes or installs a back door at the current Lead.

advantages.name: Core Command
advantages.summary: Winner executes 1 core command on the target computer (not system purge, power down, or a network change that locks a user out).
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: 1 more core command.

advantages.name: Elude
advantages.summary: Trace software aimed at the winner has its Power Rating cut by 3 until the end of next round (never more than 3 total).
advantages.repeat: Each further pick extends the effect 1 more round.

advantages.name: Extract File
advantages.summary: Winner pulls 1 chosen file from an opponent's target computer; an unknown file name/location needs an Investigation/Research check, and overruns give -4 to hacking checks.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: 1 more file.

advantages.name: Lead
advantages.summary: Lead moves 1 point toward the winner.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks in the round move Lead 1 more point toward the winner.

advantages.name: Pause
advantages.summary: Conflict freezes: Lead stays put and no steps resolve next round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds 1 more paused round.

advantages.name: Probe
advantages.summary: A chosen opponent makes a Computers (Int) check, DC 10 + 5 x winner's Probe software Power Rating; on failure the winner runs 1 core command. Opponent may skip the check, giving the winner 2 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick raises the DC by 5.

advantages.name: Seize Control
advantages.summary: Winner makes the target computer run or stop 1 program stored on either machine, or takes over 1 controlled device until Step 2 of next round.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick: control of 1 more program or device.

advantages.name: Silhouette
advantages.summary: Prey either deletes one of the Predator's back doors or builds a profile silhouette; each silhouette gives a cumulative +1 on hacking opposed checks against that Predator for the mission.

advantages.name: Stress
advantages.summary: Everyone except the winner takes 1d4 stress damage that cannot be recovered until the hacking attempt ends.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick adds +1d4 stress damage.

advantages.name: Trace
advantages.summary: A chosen opponent makes a Computers (Int) check, DC 10 + 5 x winner's Trace software Power Rating; on failure his physical location is found and a winning Prey may end the hack in his favor. Skipping gives the winner 2 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick raises the DC by 5.

advantages.name: Victory
advantages.summary: Conflict ends immediately in the winner's favor.

victory.predator: Hacker gains full control and may use any core command freely; the former defender must hack the system back as Predator to retake it.
victory.prey: Intruder is locked out and cannot hack this system again this mission.

hacking.outsideActions: Not detailed separately; when run alongside combat, Step 4 is spread over the combat round with each participant acting on his Initiative Count.

hackTiming.title: Table 6.6: Hack Timing
notes: Round duration by current Lead and access type; multiply by the Relative Power Ratings factor (hackTimingRelativePower). Both sides must be involved for at least half this time (rounded down, minimum 1 round).

hackTimingRelativePower.title: Table 6.6: Hack Timing (Relative Power Ratings)
notes: * Rounded up (minimum 1 half action).

coreCommands.title: Core Commands (text list, not a numbered table)
notes: Extract File / Upload Program: full rounds = Complexity DC / lowest Power Rating of the two computers (rounded down, minimum 1); unknown Complexity DC is GC-assigned, 10 to 60.
Initiate System Purge: 1 minute + 1 minute per foreign program whose Power Rating exceeds the system's.
Search System: 1 full action to start, then time per Table 2.33: Research Checks; no check needed; one system per use.
Use Peripheral: -4 on any separate skill check for remote operation.
View File: 1 half action to open; read 1 page per full round + 1 per point of Intelligence and of Wisdom above 10.
Unmonitored system (or streamlined variant at GC option): a Complex Task with Challenges = system Power Rating, Computers (Int) DC = known Sys-Op's Computers bonus + 10, or Threat Level + 15 if none.
External Access is any indirect connection; Internal Access is a terminal wired straight into the system and is much faster.
A terminal on the target system is assumed to have Power Rating = system's - 2 (minimum 1) unless stated otherwise.
Several participants form a Predator group and a Prey group; each makes one cooperative opposed check per round.
A blank "skill" means the default Computers (Int); alternate skill checks have no tags.
Software requirements (Trace, Probe) are recorded in "other". Probe/Trace DCs scale with the winner's software Power Rating.
Back doors set the starting Lead of later hacks; silhouettes give the defender a cumulative +1 per silhouette against that hacker for the mission. Each can be spent to erase the other.
A successful trace by the Prey can end the hack in his favor and is enough to start a manhunt.
With simultaneous combat: Step 1 before the first Initiative Count, Steps 2-3 at the Predator's count.
Master Cracker winner spends 1 use of the class ability to choose any 1 Advantage, +1 per 4 margin, never Victory.

infiltration.name: Infiltration

startingLead.summary: Organization's Image Rating if the Predator opens low profile; its History Rating if he opens high profile.

Predator opens with a high profile approach

advantages.name: Crisis
advantages.summary: Predator rolls Impress (Cha) vs. DC 25 + organization's two highest Ratings; Prey rolls Security (Int) vs. DC 25 + Predator's career level. If exactly one fails, the other wins. A side may skip its check, giving the opponent 3 Lead.
advantages.repeat: Each further pick lowers the winner's own Crisis DC by 4 (minimum 20).

advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: +1 more to the lowest identity.

advantages.name: Free Time
advantages.summary: Predator is unobserved for 1 hour. If he leaves and is late back, he needs Bluff (Cha) DC 20 + 4 x Goals Rating or the Prey wins and gains action dice equal to Lead for hostile events.
advantages.repeat: Every 2 further picks: 1 more hour (maximum 3 hours).

advantages.name: Haste
advantages.summary: Next Conflict round takes half the standard time (rounded down, minimum 5 minutes).
